description:
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 için devasa bir 3D Ötegezegen Keşif ve Hayatta Kalma Simülasyonu geliştiriyoruz! Projemizde NASA'nın gerçek Exoplanet Archive verilerini prosedürel algoritmalarla birleştirerek oyunculara 50+ farklı gezegende hayatta kalma ve anlık atmosfer/radyasyon analizi yapma imkanı sunuyoruz.

Ekibimize projenin kodlama altyapısını güçlendirecek, oyun motoru (Unity/Godot) süreçlerine destek olacak veya UI/UX arayüz tasarımında yardımcı olabilecek takım arkadaşları arıyoruz
summary: CEZERI ROBOTICS: Space Mission is an interactive 3D browser game that enables students and space enthusiasts to design and experience space missions firsthand rather than passively watching videos. Satellites monitor Earth's crops, water, droughts, and wildfires from orbit to protect human life—and today's youth will design these future systems. In the game, players plan their own missions, choose from three authentic NASA rockets (Saturn V, Falcon 9, NASA SLS), complete pre-launch system checks, and fly to 110 celestial targets, including 10 Solar System bodies and 100 of the most Earth-like exoplanets. On planetary surfaces, players scan science points and collect mineral samples, and they can also enter realistic interior modules of the International Space Station (ISS) to complete orbital tasks. Built as a single offline-ready HTML file requiring no installation or internet connection, it brings accessible, hands-on space education directly into classrooms.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

CEZERI ROBOTICS: Space Mission is a 3D web-based educational simulation that turns the entire lifecycle of a space mission into 11 sequential, playable tasks. Players progress step-by-step through mission design, rocket selection (Saturn V, Falcon 9 / Crew Dragon, or NASA SLS), spacesuit preparation, flight tag removal, propellant loading, pre-launch systems check, rocket launch, spaceflight navigation, planetary landing, surface science scanning and sample collection, International Space Station (ISS) interior module missions, and reading the final mission report. Poor engineering choices make the mission harder, teaching players why accurate technical decisions matter.

Benefits & Intended Impact

The project transforms abstract aerospace engineering and astronomy concepts into active, experiential learning. It aims to spark high school and middle school students' interest in space technologies, teach mission-planning logic, and promote educational equity. As our next step, we plan to have high school students play the simulation and complete identical short pre- and post-mission assessments to measure learning gains.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

- Programming & Web Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), and Three.js (WebGL) 3D graphics engine.

- Architecture: Self-contained single HTML file with embedded 3D models and planetary textures, running 100% offline with zero installation required.

- Design & Accessibility Factors: Optimized to run smoothly even on low-spec school computers, featuring a clean sequential checklist (toggled via the Q key) and gamified mechanics grounded in real NASA datasets.
